Please audit the next instance from curation agent:
===start
vitamins_top5_food_sources staged — ready for audit

  Adapted seed #4 (expanded from "top 3 dishes high in vitamin C" to "5 food sources for each of 6 major
   vitamins"). All cycles 1+2+3 lessons applied upfront.

  Files written:
  - datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.csv (30 rows × 5 cols)
  - datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.draft.json
  - datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.curation.json

  Schema: Vitamin(key) | List Position(numeric, non-key) | Food(key) | Approximate Content(text) |
  Source Type(categorical). Composite PK = (Vitamin, Food).

  Universe + value sources (7 Wikipedia URLs):
  - 1 vitamin-universe anchor: "Vitamin" (confirms 13-vitamin classification; staged 6 = all 4
  fat-soluble + B12 + C)
  - 6 per-vitamin articles (Vitamin A, B12, C, D, E, K) serving as both discipline-membership universe +
   value source for their respective rows

  Per-vitamin top-5 picks (descending content where article ranks numerically):
  - Vitamin A: Cod liver oil, Beef liver, Chicken liver, Sweet potato, Carrot
  - Vitamin B12: Beef liver, Clams, Crab meat, Salmon, Fortified cereal (qualitative content — article
  has no numeric table)
  - Vitamin C: Kakadu plum, Camu camu, Acerola, Indian gooseberry, Rose hip
  - Vitamin D: Rainbow trout, Sockeye salmon, UV-mushrooms, Fortified plant milk, Fortified cow milk
  (per-serving units)
  - Vitamin E: Wheat germ oil, Hazelnut oil, Sunflower oil, Almond oil, Safflower oil
  - Vitamin K: Nattō, Egg yolk, Goose meat, Butter, Hard cheese

  Source Type distribution: Animal 11 / Plant 13 / Fortified 3 / Fermented 1.

  Three documented risks (in pre-gate verdict):
  1. "Notable" framing instead of "top" (cycles 1-3 lesson applied)
  2. Vitamin B12 article has no numeric content table — 5 B12 rows preserve the article's qualitative
  descriptors with a "qualitative" tag
  3. Unit variation across vitamins (mg/100g, μg/100g, μg RAE/100g, IU/serving) — Approximate Content is
   text type

  Creator preflight: 26/26 OK including 3 cycles-1+2+3-lessons-upfront checks (PK on entity-key, List
  Position non-key numeric, "notable" not "top" framing) + Source Type categorical-vocabulary check + no
   duplicate foods.

  Domain diversity update: Food/Nutrition is now represented (NEW family). Coverage of
  domain_taxonomy.md families: 11/16 (was 10/16). Unrepresented: Law, Transportation, Environment,
  Education, Society.

  Ready for audit. Three open questions documented for the auditor: (1) qualitative B12 content cells,
  (2) unit variation across vitamins, (3) D's per-serving rather than per-100g reporting.
===end

Full pre-registration sweep: NOT READY — 2 BLOCKING findings.

Counts by severity: BLOCKING=2 / NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE=1 / SUGGESTION=1
Counts by issue type: factual=0 / structural=3 / scope-related=1

What passes:
- Local table mechanics: 30 rows x 5 columns; exactly five rows per vitamin; List Position values are 1-5 inside each vitamin; duplicate count for primary_key=(Vitamin, Food) is 0.
- Schema and metadata mechanics: CSV header matches draft.columns; column_types cover exactly the five columns; source_count=7 equals len(source_urls); query_category=scaled_enumeration and operation_type=union+filter are plausible; gt_construction=manual_wikipedia; domain=Food/Nutrition fits the taxonomy.
- The six-vitamin universe is source-grounded as a curated subset of the 13 vitamins listed by the Vitamin article. The source lists A, B12, C, D, E, and K among the 13 vitamins (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin, vitamin list, lines 268-281).
- Numeric row-value support is strong for Vitamin A, C, D, and E samples. Vitamin A supports cod liver oil, cooked beef liver, cooked chicken liver, baked sweet potato, and cooked carrot with the staged values (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_A, Sources table, lines 520-545). Vitamin C supports the five staged plant sources and values (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_C, Plant sources table, lines 451-458). Vitamin D supports the staged per-serving values for trout, sockeye salmon, UV-exposed mushrooms, fortified milk, and fortified plant milks (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_D, Food sources table, lines 639-653). Vitamin E supports the five staged oils and values (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_E, Sources table, lines 344-352).

Findings:

1. (structural, BLOCKING) The Vitamin B12 rows do not all have exact food-name and Approximate Content support from the cited Vitamin_B12 article.

CSV rows 7-11 use the Vitamin_B12 article as the only value source for five B12 rows. That source supports broad categories and a few exact items: liver/organ meats including beef, shellfish, crab meat, breakfast cereals as fortified foods, and a bioavailability statement for fish/fowl/meat. It does not surface the exact food names “Clams” or “Salmon” in the cited section, and the Salmon cell uses a bioavailability percentage rather than an approximate content value. Staged source locator: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_B12, Animal-derived foods and Fortified foods, lines 404-420. Local locators: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.csv lines 7-11; curation.json source_coverage_notes source_urls[2].

The documented “qualitative B12” caveat is honest, but it does not fully repair the row-value contract: the row-level Food values still need to be recoverable from the cited URL, and the Approximate Content column should not silently switch from content to absorption/bioavailability for one exact food. This is analogous to the earlier missing value-role source problem in the inventions instance.

Minimal repair: either replace the unsupported exact foods with the exact source-level categories (“shellfish”, “fish”) and rename/describe the content column accordingly, or add reliable per-food / nutrition-table sources for exact B12 foods and values. If adding per-food sources supplies the load-bearing values, update source_urls, source_count, source roles, claim_type/source plan if needed, and the B12 normalization notes.

2. (scope-related, BLOCKING) The Vitamin K partition is framed as broad “Vitamin K” but the staged row set is a K2-only subset.

The CSV rows 27-31 are Nattō, Egg yolk, Goose meat, Butter, and Hard cheese under Vitamin K. Those values come from the article’s Vitamin K2 subsection, not from a broad Vitamin K food-source selection. The same Vitamin K source page lists high K1 plant sources immediately above, including collard greens, spinach, turnip greens, kale, and broccoli, with much larger listed K1 amounts than the animal K2 foods. Staged source locator: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_K, K1 food sources and K2 subsection, lines 258-326. Local locators: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.csv lines 27-31; curation.json source_coverage_notes source_urls[6], which itself says leafy greens dominate K1 while the staged rows are from the K2 list.

This materially affects scope because a model asked for notable food sources for “Vitamin K” would reasonably return the broad K1-rich leafy-green sources from the same cited article. The staged table instead evaluates a narrower K2-rich food subset without exposing that subset in the Vitamin key, title, or query contract.

Minimal repair: either retitle/rekey the partition to make the target “Vitamin K2” explicit, or replace the Vitamin K rows with broad Vitamin K sources from the cited article and update the Approximate Content units/Source Type values. If the K2 subset is retained, scrub the title, temporal_note, extraction notes, source roles, and decision_log so the benchmark question no longer implies broad Vitamin K.

3. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Source Type distribution is misstated in both the handoff and draft extraction notes.

The CSV has Source Type counts Animal=13, Plant=13, Fortified=3, Fermented=1. draft.json::_extraction_notes says “Animal 11 rows” even while the parenthetical breakdown A:3 + B12:4 + D:2 + K:4 sums to 13. Local locators: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.csv Source Type column; datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.draft.json line 42.

Minimal cleanup: change Animal 11 to Animal 13 in the handoff/current-state narrative and any preflight text copied into audit_response.

4. (structural, SUGGESTION) secondary_category=top_k is fragile for the current framing.

The primary category scaled_enumeration is correct, and the title has already been softened to “notable.” But secondary_category is still top_k even though B12 is qualitative and the K partition currently uses a subtype selection. Local locator: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/vitamins_top5_food_sources.draft.json lines 22-24. If repairs keep a strictly ranked content table for every vitamin, top_k can remain. If repairs keep selected/notable subset framing, consider dropping the secondary_category or documenting that top_k applies only to numeric per-vitamin display order where the source table supports it.

Final judgment: Not ready. The table is mechanically clean and most numeric vitamin partitions are well grounded, but B12 exact row support and the Vitamin K/K2 scope mismatch block registration.

Minimal fixes needed:
1. Repair B12 exact food/value support by adding exact sources or changing the row values to what the cited article actually states.
2. Repair the Vitamin K scope mismatch by either making K2 explicit or replacing rows with broad Vitamin K sources.
3. Correct the Animal Source Type distribution from 11 to 13.
4. Revisit secondary_category=top_k after deciding whether the repaired table is genuinely ranked or selected/notable.
5. Append audit_response.cycle_1 and rerun preflight.
